title: Physical quantities: magnitude and unit practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: Contexts, wording, values and planned diagrams are newly authored. The two mapped P2 leaves inform only the demand to report a calculated magnitude with its unit.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: identification to calculation, comparison and integrated record correction
question_set_contract.dependency_exception: This is the first lesson of the first AS Physics topic. No previous lesson or module exists, so no dependency pair is fabricated.

questions.prompt: State the two parts that make up every physical quantity.
Which entry is a complete reported value of a physical quantity?
A stopwatch record is 5 s and a ribbon record is 5 m. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The records are identical because both magnitudes are 5.
options.B: The magnitudes are equal, but the different units show that the records describe different quantities.
options.C: The units are equal, but the magnitudes are different.
options.D: Neither record is complete because each contains only one unit.

questions.prompt: A mass calculation gives a numerical magnitude of 0.75, and the stated unit is kg. A student records 0.75 m. Which correction is valid?

options.A: Keep 0.75 m because the numerical magnitude is correct.
options.B: Write 0.75 kg because 0.75 is the magnitude and kg is the stated unit.
options.C: Write kg because the unit is enough without a magnitude.
options.D: Write 0.75 because a calculated number needs no unit.

questions.prompt: The diagram shows identical sample jars together on a balance. Use the information in the diagram to calculate the mass of one jar. Then identify the numerical magnitude and the unit in your result, and explain why writing only the number would be incomplete.

figure.purpose: Assess extraction of an equal-share calculation from a simple visual record
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white line drawing of five identical unlabelled sample jars together on a balance. Label only the total balance reading 3.5 kg and the fact that the jars are identical. Do not show division or the single-jar result.
figure.alt_text: Five identical sample jars together have a total mass of 3.5 kg.

questions.prompt: A school record contains a duration of 3 s and a length of 3 m. Compare their numerical magnitudes and units. Explain why the two records do not describe the same physical quantity and why each complete record needs both of its parts.

A technician checks two records. Six identical metal pieces have a total mass of 0.84 kg, and four equal timing intervals have a total duration of 10 s. The technician records one piece as 0.84 with no unit and one interval as 10 kg. Calculate and write both single-item records correctly. For each original entry, identify the numerical error and the unit error.

figure.purpose: Assess integrated calculation and diagnosis of missing-unit and wrong-unit records

Panel two shows four equal clock intervals, total 10 s and flawed draft single-interval entry 10 kg. Do not show corrections or final answers.
